1) Failure modes now covered by retraining (mostly NOT the scored task)  
- Single-instruction prompts with strict “exactly N items” constraints, over- or under-producing items (1,4–6,8,10).  
- Single-instruction prompts with required output format or fields (JSON vs plain text, fixed schema) violated (2,4,7).  
- Style/genre sub-constraint acknowledged as not met (3).  
- One genuine multi-question completeness miss: answers only first of two numbered requests (9).  

2) Conversation types already handled correctly  
- No additional info beyond prior note: single-instruction, constraint-focused prompts are broadly well understood; several such negatives already scored correctly this cycle.  

3) High-value regions to probe next (within multi-question “completeness” task)  
- Prompts like: “1) List X; 2) Transform each item…”, where reply covers all items but drops the transform step.  
- Prompts asking 3–4 heterogeneous sub-questions (definition + example + comparison) with partial omissions.  
- Cases where every sub-question is answered but counts/formats are wrong vs. ones with perfect counts but a missing sub-question.
